clue.text: Climbing large tree? Pack good old anorak

indicators.note: the climbing letters pack, or hold inside them, the next two pieces
in a down entry, climbing means the large tree pair is written upwards, back to front

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
an oak is a tree

explanation.surface: A climber heading up a big tree is told to take a trusty old waterproof jacket along.
explanation.definitionFit: A kagool (cagoule) is a lightweight hooded waterproof jacket, a kind of anorak.

clue.text: Trustworthy sort not entirely following rugby's code of conduct?

indicators.note: the trimmed trustworthy sort comes after, following, the rugby letters

parts.note: RU is the abbreviation for Rugby Union

indicators.note: the word for a trustworthy sort is not given entirely: its last letter is dropped

parts.note: a brick is a reliable, trustworthy person in British slang

explanation.surface: A reliable chap not quite keeping to the sporting etiquette of rugby.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'brick' is old British slang for a dependable, good-hearted person; lose its final K.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubric is a set of rules or instructions, as for conduct in a church service or an exam.

clue.text: "With this ring … as long as we both …"?

definitions.text: "With this ring … as long as we both …"?

parts.words: "With this ring … as long as we both …"?
parts.note: the wedding-vow fragments suggest a ring that lasts as long as the couple shall live

explanation.walkthrough: The marriage vows run 'With this ring I thee wed' and 'as long as we both shall live': a ring, or circle, for life. The phrase is also the song from The Lion King.
explanation.definitionFit: The circle of life is the idea of an endless cycle of birth and death, here punned as a lifelong wedding ring.

clue.text: Grounds for drilling sandbank shelf — 9 & 25?

parts.note: a bar is a sandbank across a river mouth or harbour
a rack is a framework of shelves
9 and 25 are both square numbers, three squared and five squared

explanation.surface: Seemingly about where to drill for oil on a sandbank or continental shelf, with two cross-references.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drilling' suggests oil rigs, but it means military drill. The numbers 9 and 25 also point to the entries ICICLE and HOT WATER, but here they just mean square numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Barrack squares are the parade grounds where soldiers practise marching drill.

clue.text: Undoubtedly this examinee's at a loss!

definitions.meaning: second meaning, read literally: a candidate with no question in front of them has nothing to answer

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is read literally for the examinee: someone without a question is stuck.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means certainly or beyond dispute; literally it describes someone lacking a question to answer.

clue.text: Italian passing over 0-0 is 1-0 up — ace!

indicators.note: the reversed one-nil letters pass over, wrapping round, the next piece
in a down entry, up means the one-nil letters are written upwards, back to front

parts.note: one-zip: I is one in Roman numerals and zip means nil
read as a sum, 'zero' minus '0', where the second nought is the letter O
A is the abbreviation for ace on playing cards

explanation.surface: A football report: an Italian side goes 1-0 up after a goalless spell, and someone cheers.
explanation.walkthrough: The scores are not results but sums and readings: '1-0' is one-zip, and '0-0' is nought take away nought. The Italian is a restaurant, not a team.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian, in everyday speech, is an Italian restaurant, and a pizzeria is one.

clue.text: Barrier protecting my city

indicators.note: the barrier protects by surrounding the exclamation

parts.note: a fence is a barrier
'Lor!' is an old exclamation of surprise, like 'My!'

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of a wall that protects their home town.
explanation.definitionFit: Florence is the Tuscan capital, one of Italy's great Renaissance cities.

clue.text: Animals replaced in launcher by ex-POTUS's granny

indicators.note: the animals are swapped out of the launcher for the president

parts.note: a bazooka is a rocket launcher
a zoo is a collection of animals
Bush, either George, is a former President of the United States

explanation.surface: A former US president's grandmother, with some zoo animals and a rocket launcher thrown in.
explanation.definitionFit: Babushka is the Russian word for grandmother, also used for an old Russian woman in a headscarf.

clue.text: I, the Reaper, caught one frozen in suspense

indicators.note: caught as in heard or picked up by ear, so the word is a sound-alike

parts.note: the Grim Reaper carries a scythe or sickle, so the reaper's tool is a sickle

explanation.surface: Death introduces himself and claims a victim stuck in limbo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One frozen in suspense' looks like a thriller victim, but it means a hanging spike of ice.
explanation.definitionFit: An icicle is ice that has frozen while dripping, hanging down from an edge.

clue.text: Rust on surface — will nothing stop it?

definitions.text: Rust on surface — will nothing stop it?

indicators.note: the nothing goes in to stop up the gap between the two outer letters
only the surface of the word, its outside letters, is used

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A worried owner sees corrosion spreading and asks whether anything can halt it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rot is decay and corrosion, the sort of creeping damage rust does to a surface.

clue.text: On wheels, lout taking a spin

definitions.text: On wheels, lout taking a spin

indicators.note: the whole string spins round, read from end to start

parts.note: re means on, concerning
a car is a set of wheels in slang
yob is British slang for a lout

explanation.surface: A young thug goes out for a drive.
explanation.walkthrough: A yob is a British hooligan.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy racer is a young man who drives fast and showily, a loutish figure behind the wheel.

clue.text: Literary outsiders thwart cruel trap

indicators.note: thwart means across, so the outsiders sit across the middle of the cruel word

parts.note: hard means harsh, cruel
the outsiders of the letters, the alphabet, are its first and last, A and Z

explanation.surface: Fringe writers foil a vicious snare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Literary' is read as 'of letters': the alphabet runs from A to Z.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf a hazard, such as a bunker, is a trap; more broadly it is a danger or pitfall.

clue.text: "I" put in CATHOLIC with "I" put in IN

parts.note: to elect is to put in office by vote

indicators.note: the second I is put in the Catholic letters

parts.note: RC is the abbreviation for Roman Catholic
in, meaning fashionable, is current

explanation.surface: Reads like a coded instruction to insert a letter into two capitalised words.
explanation.walkthrough: The first "I" is the definition: physicists use I as the symbol for current.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics equations such as V = IR, the letter I stands for the flow of charge in a circuit.

clue.text: I run through Devon base by base

parts.note: e is the base of natural logarithms
x means by, as in 3 x 4
e again, the natural-log base

explanation.surface: A runner describes a cross-country route through Devon, going from one base to the next.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'I' is the river speaking. Devon is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Exe is a river flowing through Devon to the sea at Exmouth.

clue.text: Volatile sort, as lady keenly joining hadj?

indicators.note: as means behaving like the volatile sort just named, so the letters that follow are volatile, shaken up

explanation.surface: A woman who eagerly goes on the Muslim pilgrimage, the hadj, to Mecca.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition doubles as the anagram signal: 'as' says LADY KEENLY + HADJ behave like a volatile sort.
explanation.definitionFit: From Stevenson's tale of a man with two personalities, the phrase describes someone of wildly unpredictable temperament.

clue.text: Singer of folk jazz organised a beano for Azed in the auditorium?

indicators.note: the rearranged party goes in place of the two letters

parts.note: taken as written; the A and Z in its middle are the letters swapped out

indicators.note: in an auditorium you hear things, so the name is taken by its sound

parts.note: the name sounds like 'A, zed', the letters A and Z
the letters of a beano, a party, organised into a new order

explanation.surface: A jazz musician throws a party for Azed, the Observer crossword setter.
explanation.walkthrough: Azed is the long-running Observer crossword setter; his name sounds like 'A, zed'.
explanation.definitionFit: Joan Baez is an American folk singer known for protest songs of the 1960s.

clue.text: Receive a thousand extra thanks for turning up at waterway

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means the pieces are written upwards, back to front
the thousand comes as an extra piece after the thanks

parts.note: to get is to receive
ta is British informal for thanks
K stands for a thousand

explanation.surface: Someone gets a big tip and extra gratitude for arriving at a canal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kattegat is the strait, a sea passage, between Denmark and Sweden.

clue.text: See 4
Gentleman of the road reported bitter whisky

definitions.meaning: a rye is a Romany gentleman, as in George Borrow's The Romany Rye
rye is a whisky distilled from rye grain

indicators.note: reported means said aloud, so the word for bitter is taken by its sound

parts.note: wry means twisted, bitter, sardonic

explanation.surface: A tramp says his whiskey tastes sour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gentleman of the road' suggests a tramp, but it is the Romany word for a gentleman.
explanation.definitionFit: Rye is the Romani word for a gentleman, and also a North American grain spirit.

clue.text: See 15
Under review then, for a few, the onset of change?

definitions.text: Under review then, for a few, the onset of change?

indicators.note: the words under review are revised, reworked into a new order
the onset of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Being observed, some people begin to alter their behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: Named after studies at the Hawthorne Works factory, where workers' output changed simply because they were being watched.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hawthorne effect is the tendency of people to modify behaviour when they know they are being studied.

clue.text: Traditionally plated karahi gosht, perhaps, served fiery hot?

indicators.note: the meat is plated, served in the iron pan

parts.note: a karahi is a cooking pan traditionally made of iron, chemical symbol Fe
gosht is the Urdu word for meat, often lamb

explanation.surface: A curry dish served in its traditional pan arrives sizzling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Traditionally' says the karahi, an Indian wok, is classically made of iron.
explanation.definitionFit: Flambé describes food doused in spirit and set alight before serving.

clue.text: Regularly curse folly with a touch of explicit language

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of each word
a touch is just a little, the first letter

explanation.surface: Someone swears often at a silly act, with a bit of crude language.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the odd letters of curse and the even letters of folly.
explanation.definitionFit: A creole is a language formed when a pidgin becomes the native tongue of a community.

clue.text: Muscles are adversely affected, it's said, after one?

indicators.note: it's said means spoken aloud, a sound-alike

parts.note: abs are the stomach muscles; to ail is to be adversely affected, unwell

explanation.surface: Muscles ache afterwards, apparently, after a single go at something.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads 'after one' as going down after a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: To abseil is to descend a cliff on a rope, following one down.

clue.text: Sadly what monarch losing crown got in

definitions.text: Sadly what monarch losing crown got in

indicators.note: the shortened word goes in among the rearranged letters
sadly means badly, so the word what is rearranged
losing its crown means losing its top, first letter

parts.note: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A deposed king lamented the trouble he had landed in.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot water is trouble, the predicament of a monarch who has lost the throne.

clue.text: Her mirror image cherished by Henry VIII

indicators.note: a mirror image is back to front, so these letters are read in reverse
cherished by means held within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A wife's reflection treasured by the much-married Tudor king.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivy is a girl's name, so it can stand for a woman, her.

clue.text: Fat chap's clutched back part

indicators.note: back means the result is read in reverse
the fat clutches the chap, holding him inside

parts.note: flab is body fat
he is a chap; the 's stands for has

explanation.surface: A portly man has his back seized.
explanation.definitionFit: Behalf is one's side or part, as in 'on my part' meaning 'on my behalf'.

clue.text: Favourite in nursery has nobbled Ebor ringer

indicators.note: the doll has, holds, the nobbled letters inside

parts.note: a doll is a favourite toy in a nursery

indicators.note: nobbled means tampered with, so the race name is rearranged

explanation.surface: A horse-racing scandal: the favourite has been doped before the Ebor, a big race at York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Favourite' and 'nursery' sound like racing (a nursery is a race for two-year-olds), but this is a child's toy.
explanation.definitionFit: A doorbell is something that rings, a ringer, at the front door.
